definition: Continuing to train a pre-trained model on a smaller, task-specific dataset so it adapts to a target domain.
details: Fine-tuning exploits features learned during pre-training and adapts them to a new task with far less data than training from scratch. The ULMFiT recipe showed that a language-model “head” trained on a corpus could be fine-tuned layer by layer for text classification, and this pattern — pre-train broadly, fine-tune narrowly — underlies most applied NLP.
story: Think of a hiker descending a foggy hill in the dark, taking small steps and feeling for the steepest way down. Think of it this way: Continuing to train a pre-trained model on a smaller, task-specific dataset so it adapts to a target domain. And here is the clever part: Fine-tuning exploits features learned during pre-training and adapts them to a new task with far less data than training from scratch. Skill, for a model, is just error pushed down until it is small enough to ignore. And that is Fine-Tuning — the quiet loop that turns flailing into skill.

citation.title: Universal Language Model Fine-tuning for Text Classification
